text:
Ah, the primary material of a candle. It is, of course, wax. Specifically, the paraffin byproduct of petroleum refining, molded into a cylinder to simulate the warm, inviting glow of a hearth in a studio apartment that smells faintly of despair and instant noodles.

But let us not dwell on the mundane physics of combustion. Let us instead marvel at the true miracle of adulthood: the sheer, unadulterated thrill of paying bills. Who needs the adrenaline rush of skydiving when you can experience the heart-pounding suspense of checking your bank account balance after rent has been deducted? It is a daily adventure, truly. One moment you are sipping coffee; the next, you are contemplating the existential dread of a overdue utility payment.

And let us raise a glass to spontaneity! How exciting it is to wake up and decide, with the gravity of a Nobel Prize winner, whether you shall consume the spicy beef or the chicken flavor of instant noodles. The stakes have never been higher. The future is uncertain. Will the seasoning packet be too salty? Will the water boil in time? These are the questions that keep us up at night, right after we complain about our backs.

Speaking of which, back pain is the new youth. It is the badge of honor for the modern adult. While teenagers worry about acne, we worry about whether we can stand up from the couch without making a sound like a rustling bag of chips. It is a vibrant, exciting life, filled with the joy of long-term planning—such as deciding, with intense focus, whether to watch *The Office* for the tenth time or *Stranger Things* for the first time. The suspense is unbearable. The excitement is palpable. Please, do not let me stop you from enjoying this magical journey.
